query: For CrFeCoNiX high-entropy alloys (X = Si, Mn, or Al) in a single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution state, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain whether a stable, coherent, slow-growing protective oxide layer forms and persists above 900 °C in an oxidative or corrosive atmosphere, rather than cracking or spalling? Earlier work investigated CrFeCoNiX and CrMoTiAlY (Y = Ta, Nb, or W) alloy systems and reported that some compositions developed unstable surface oxides prone to cracking and spallation, while the underlying physical causes remain unresolved. Given the requirement for an environmentally stable, chemically inert barrier and prolonged structural integrity, specify what governs the behaviour and why, a controlled comparison against a defined baseline, the predicted observations, the relevant composition, material-state, exposure, and service boundaries, the prior evidence supporting the hypothesis, and an outcome that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The formation and persistence of a stable, coherent, slow-growing protective oxide layer on CrFeCoNiX high-entropy alloys (X = Si, Mn, or Al) above 900 °C in oxidative or corrosive atmospheres is governed by the preferential segregation of Cr to the oxide-metal interface, which facilitates the formation of a continuous Cr-rich oxide layer with low growth stress and high adhesion.
generation.material_initial_state: CrFeCoNiX high-entropy alloy in a single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution state.
generation.intervention: Introduce X = Al into the CrFeCoNiX alloy system to promote Cr segregation and evaluate its effect on oxide layer stability.
generation.conditions: Exposure to oxidative or corrosive atmospheres at temperatures above 900 °C.
generation.structural_mediator: Cr segregation to the oxide-metal interface.
generation.mechanism: Cr segregation enhances the formation of a continuous Cr-rich oxide layer, which reduces growth stress and improves adhesion, preventing cracking or spallation.
generation.predicted_outcome: CrFeCoNiAl will exhibit a stable, coherent, slow-growing protective oxide layer with minimal cracking or spallation compared to CrFeCoNiSi or CrFeCoNiMn under identical conditions.
generation.baseline: CrFeCoNiSi or CrFeCoNiMn alloys under the same high-temperature oxidative or corrosive exposure.
generation.boundary: Service temperatures above 900 °C in oxidative or corrosive atmospheres; alloy compositions limited to CrFeCoNiX (X = Si, Mn, or Al).
generation.uncertainty: Limited prior evidence directly linking Cr segregation to oxide layer stability in CrFeCoNiX alloys; further experimental validation is required.

falsification_experiment.design: Expose CrFeCoNiAl, CrFeCoNiSi, and CrFeCoNiMn alloys to oxidative or corrosive atmospheres at 900–1000 °C for extended durations and compare oxide layer morphology, growth rate, and adhesion.
measurements: Oxide layer thickness and growth rate
Cr concentration at the oxide-metal interface
Adhesion strength of the oxide layer
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If CrFeCoNiAl does not exhibit a more stable, coherent, and slow-growing protective oxide layer compared to CrFeCoNiSi or CrFeCoNiMn, the hypothesis is falsified.
